n: In August 1830, Joseph was on his way to buy wine for a sacrament meeting when a heavenly messenger met him. Jesus Christ introduces himself as Lord, God, and Redeemer.
What we eat or drink in the sacrament doesn’t matter, as long as we partake focused on God’s glory and remembering Christ’s body and blood. This is why the Church uses water today.

f.w: an eye single to my glory
my body which was laid down for you

n: The Saints should not buy wine or strong drink from their enemies — possibly a precaution against tampering.

f.g: alcoholic beverages stronger than ordinary wine.

n: They should use only wine made among themselves in God’s kingdom on earth.

A time will come when Christ will drink the fruit of the vine with his Saints on earth — a great sacrament gathering, likely at Adam-ondi-Ahman. Moroni, who holds the keys of the Book of Mormon (the “stick of Ephraim”), will be there.

f.w: drink of the fruit of the vine with you on the earth

f.g: the Book of Mormon, a record of Joseph’s descendants through Ephraim.

n: Elias, who holds keys to restore all things spoken by the prophets, will also be there.

f.g: a title meaning forerunner or restorer; it can refer to several messengers.

n: John the Baptist, son of Zacharias, came with the spirit of Elias. Elias (here likely Gabriel) promised Zacharias that he would have a son named John.
John the Baptist ordained Joseph and Oliver to the Aaronic Priesthood.

f.w: to ordain you unto the first priesthood

n: Elijah, who holds the keys of turning hearts between generations, so that the earth is not cursed, will also be present.
The patriarchs Joseph, Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham — through whom God’s covenant promises continue — will be there.
Michael — Adam, father of all humanity and the “Ancient of Days” — will attend as well.
Peter, James, and John, who ordained Joseph and Oliver as apostles and special witnesses, will be present. This is a key reference to the restoration of the Melchizedek Priesthood.
To them Christ committed the keys of his kingdom for the last dispensation, the “fulness of times,” when all things in heaven and earth will be gathered in one.
And all those the Father has given Christ out of the world will be there too.

f.w: those whom my Father hath given me out of the world

n: So rejoice, prepare yourselves, and put on God’s whole armor to withstand evil and stand firm. Paul’s famous image follows.

f.g: tie up your long robe for action; get ready.

f.w: take upon you my whole armor

n: Stand with truth as your belt, righteousness as your breastplate, and the gospel of peace on your feet — which angels have restored.

f.w: your loins girt about with truth

n: Faith is a shield that puts out the adversary’s flaming arrows.
Put on the helmet of salvation and take the Spirit’s sword and God’s word. Be united in your prayers and faithful until he comes, and you will be with him.

f.w: where I am ye shall be also
